decisions.executionNote: Approach the basket with the left arm, raising and gradually pitching the open gripper downward; keep the right arm clear.
Track the basket's left front rim as it moves right on the conveyor; approach with open jaws without crossing the arms.
The basket has moved into the right workspace; withdraw the left arm and bring the right gripper toward its right rim.
Replan from unchanged poses after the rejected right-arm start, using smaller initial increments to preserve elbow-up continuity.
Move the right gripper forward and pitch it toward the basket's near right rim; leave the left arm on its own side for the image-matched object.
Seat the right gripper around the near right basket rim and close; verify actual basket retention by lifting next.
Lift the grasped basket 12 cm with the right gripper closed, moving slightly inward while keeping the arms separated.
Basket retention is not visually convincing. Reopen and realign over its moving right rim with a more vertical approach before retrying the lift.
Lower toward the basket rim while tracking rightward conveyor motion; smaller pitch and forward increments avoid the prior IK jump.
Adjust outward and past the near corner so the fingers straddle the right side wall, then close around the rim.
Close fully and test retention with a small upward/backward lift, easing wrist pitch to remain within continuous elbow-up IK.
The basket is still conveyor-supported. Reopen and descend farther at its outer rim, with a shallower wrist pitch and lateral tracking.
Fine-align over the outer side rim, lower the fingertips just below its top, and close while matching conveyor drift.
Allow the right jaws to finish closing at the rim, then make a small retention-test lift rather than lifting while they are still moving.
Closed fingers appear empty. Reopen and shift outward and toward the near edge to place the rim between, rather than beyond, the fingertips.
Close at the newly aligned rim and dwell for closure, then test a short lift and inward pull for visible basket retention.
Test whether the basket follows a sustained 10 cm lift and inward translation, keeping the right gripper closed.
Switch to the basket's nearer left side wall, still using only the right workspace; descend open toward the solid upper rim rather than the corner lattice.
Use wrist feedback to center the basket's left side wall between the open right fingers; it currently lies at the outer finger.
Center and lower around the basket's left wall before closing. Bring the left arm above the incoming white remote matching the board.
Finish closing around the basket wall, then test a 5 cm lift; align the open left gripper above the white remote for pickup.
The basket wall is now visibly between the right jaws. Lift backward with a shallower wrist angle to avoid the IK limit, while lowering the left gripper toward the white remote.
Reduce the initial backward-lift increments after the continuity rejection, preserving the closed basket grasp; continue the left remote approach.
Lift the retained basket another 8 cm and bring it inward. Track and close the left gripper around the white remote matching the board.
Test the remote grasp with a vertical lift and carry the closed right basket grip inward, maintaining separation and basket elevation.
The remote remained on the belt; reopen and descend farther while tracking it. Rotate the held basket toward the center without crossing the arms.
Fine-center and close the left jaws lower on the white remote, allowing closure before lifting. Continue turning the elevated basket toward the central handoff area.
The left fingertips still appear above the remote. Reopen, lower another 6 cm while tracking its motion, and finish positioning the held basket centrally.
Remote contact shifted it toward the outer left finger. Relieve the downward contact slightly, recenter laterally, and close at belt height; hold the basket steady aloft.
The white remote is centered between the left jaws. Dwell closed, then lift it up and back beside the basket to verify retention and clear the rim.
The remote visibly follows the left gripper. Raise it above the lifted basket rim while retracting slightly to maintain continuous elbow-up reach.
After the interrupted lift, use smaller upward steps with more retraction and a slightly shallower pitch to clear the basket rim without folding the elbow further.
The basket rim is contacting the left fingers. Retract away while lifting the retained remote higher, allowing the basket to settle before moving over its opening.
Move the remote inward above the rim while easing wrist pitch and retracting to avoid the reach limit. Gently level the basket with the right wrist, keeping both grasps closed.
Halve the initial left-arm increments after the continuity rejection, then gradually continue toward the opening while gently leveling the held basket.
Carry the remote over the basket's left-central opening, slightly raising its clearance. Lower the basket only 2 cm while retaining more than the required lift.
Keep the retained remote steady after the left-arm continuity limit. Shift the elevated basket underneath it using the right arm, maintaining arm separation.
The white remote is now over the basket interior. Release it, then retract the left gripper while holding the basket raised and steady.
